the application should begin speaking promptly in a calm and consistent voice,
preserve the meaning of every paragraph, pronounce unfamiliar names carefully,

Every dictation made with the owner's Super+Alt+D toggle is cleaned by
a small local CPU model (S1-mini by Superwhisper) before it lands in the clipboard,
with no server or service the owner has to install, start or maintain.
The model is loaded only when a dictation needs it and is unloaded after Handy's existing idle
timeout, so it holds no memory when unused.
Quill or any second model entry; per-shortcut presets; streaming output; GPU Vulkan inference;
linking llama.cpp into the Handy process; changes to speech transcription; upstream PR.
Binary location: llama-server (not bin, to avoid clashing with Fedora's llama-cpp package).
Resolution order: env HANDY LLAMA SERVER (dev only), then llama-server.
A missing binary is a LocalLlmError::BinaryMissing, never a panic.
It is built statically (-DBUILD SHARED LIBS=OFF,
CPU backend only) so it shares no libraries with Handy's bundled ggml.
ModelEntry { id, display name, attribution, card url, backend: BackendKind::LlamaServer, file name,
url (Hugging Face resolve URL at a pinned commit revision), sha256, size bytes,
prompt style: PromptStyle, default ctx: u32 }.
v1 entry: s1-mini-q4km, "S1-mini by Superwhisper",
file s1-mini-q4 k m gguf from superwhisper s1-mini-GGUF at a pinned revision,
size 484,219,808 bytes,
sha256 from the Hugging Face LFS oid (the planner records the exact revision and hash after
re-verifying them), PromptStyle::S1ControlLine, context 4096.
Request: POST completions with messages, temperature: 0, stream: false,
max tokens = min(2 * est tokens(input) + 64, ctx 2),
chat template kwargs: {"enable thinking": false}, bearer API key.
A dedicated reqwest client with timeout 10 s + 50 ms * input words.
Chunking: if the estimated prompt exceeds 1000 tokens (card limit per pass),
split the transcript at sentence boundaries into chunks under the limit, process them in order,
join with a single space.
Output guards, in order (any failure returns an error,
so the raw transcript is used): strip think blocks and invisible characters (existing helpers);
empty output is accepted only when the input has at most 3 words;
output with fewer than 50% of the input's words is rejected with a warning.
Shown in post-processing settings when provider is "Local (in-app)": model dropdown (registry),
Download Delete button with progress, status label (Not loaded Loading Ready Error with reason),
the three S1 dropdowns (only for S1ControlLine), attribution link. English strings only.
LocalLlmError { BinaryMissing, ModelMissing, ModelCorrupt, StartTimeout, StartFailed,
RequestTimeout, Http(status), BadOutput(reason), Failed }.
Every variant is logged at warn with its reason and maps to the raw transcript.
No new work on the main thread. No unwrap expect in non-test code.
Each guard in 4 and each lifecycle rule in 6 gets a counterfactual: disable only that guard,
show the test failing, restore.
Integration test (ignored by default, enabled with HANDY LOCAL LLM IT=1,
needs the model file and llama-server): spawns the real server, runs 3 synthetic transcripts,
asserts outputs equal golden files (greedy decoding is deterministic),
asserts the child is gone after unload().
Acceptance on the installed RPM (added to gate.sh as check 6,
owner runs it): after one Super+Alt+D dictation the Handy log shows a local-LLM success line and the
clipboard holds the cleaned text; with model unload timeout set to 2 minutes,
no llama-server process exists 2 minutes after the last dictation; with the model file removed,
a dictation still yields the raw transcript.
Make post-processing a first-class, visible part of daily use: both shortcuts in one place,
the local cleanup model managed and switched like the transcription model,
and every history entry showing whether it was cleaned and what changed.
Transcription models were checked for per-model settings: none exist.
Language, translation, custom words, accelerator,
GPU device and unload timeout are app-wide (src-tauri src settings rs:434-535),
so no transcription-model settings page is needed.
Tabs on the Models page; moving the enable switch; Quill or other models; release pipeline,
updater endpoint or signing;
translations beyond English for new strings (other locales fall back or keep existing labels);
upstream PRs.
